name: fairy bride

attributes.attribute: fell into a sleep no one could wake
returned after the mound was opened
woke after Fairyland trace was taken off

sources: Kennedy, Patrick. Legendary Fictions of the Irish Celts. New York: Benjamin Blom, 1969, 111.
Monaghan, Patricia. The Encyclopedia of Celtic Mythology and Folklore. Checkmark Books, 2008.
text: Fairy bride is a folkloric motif. Brides figure among the humans most often snatched by fairy folk. Many tales tell of a bride who returned home in her finery and sank into a sleep no one could wake. The groom usually had to find the fairy mound that held her stolen soul. There he caught her mid-dance and brought her away once more. Even at home his bride stayed asleep. Relatives searched her clothing for any wisp of Fairyland, a pin or a thread. When that token came off, she woke at once. A few stories snare young grooms on the way to a wedding through the tricks of fairy lovers. Brides sat at much greater risk.

okr.objective: Fairy bride is a folkloric motif in which a wedding day brings fairy peril.
key_results: Brides rank high among fairy kidnapping victims.
A bride sank into a sleep no one could wake.
Her groom had to retrieve her soul from the Fairy Mound.
Removing a pin or thread of Fairyland woke her.
